meta.title: AstraZeneca + BMS: Portfolio Fit or Collision?
meta.lateStageDefinition: Unique lead investigational asset in Phase II or Phase III/pivotal/registration development; approved-indication expansions and major lifecycle-management programs excluded.
meta.countDefinition: Distinct shared indication territories, modality classes, target/mechanism themes, or stage bands; not all possible asset-pair permutations.
meta.launchDisclaimer: Illustrative analyst scenario based on trial primary-completion timing and a stage-specific lag. Not company guidance or a probability-adjusted forecast.
meta.salesDisclaimer: Investigational assets have no historical sales. Commercial benchmarks are company-reported worldwide brand revenue and are generally not indication-specific.
meta.matrixDefinition: Analyst-normalized indication-territory by modality-family map. AZ-only and BMS-only cells represent complementarity in the matched late-stage snapshot; split cells represent overlap. The map does not capture earlier-stage, marketed, or undisclosed programs.
meta.commercialUpdate: Reported sales through H1 2026; projections are transparent analyst scenarios that incorporate disclosed loss-of-exclusivity dates.

overlapUnits.rationale: Multiple programs from both companies are being developed in NSCLC, creating direct disease-level overlap.
Both companies have late-stage prostate-cancer programs, although targets and modalities differ.
Both use oral/small-molecule targeted approaches in solid tumors.
Both have late-stage dual-target immuno-oncology biologics.
Both have substantial ADC activity, with AstraZeneca contributing greater breadth.
Both have targeted radiopharmaceutical programs, but in different tumor types and targets.
Both portfolios use PD-1/PD-L1-centered combinations or multispecific approaches.
Both have EGFR-directed ADC programs, paired with different second targets.
Both companies have Phase II programs in the disease area.
Both have broad Phase III/registration portfolios in solid tumors.
Both companies have multiple late-stage programs in multiple myeloma.
Both have Phase III programs in B-cell lymphoma territories.
Both have autologous CAR-T programs in multiple myeloma, with different target configurations.
Both use small-molecule targeted approaches, but mechanisms and disease emphasis differ.
This is the clearest exact target overlap: an ADC versus CAR-T directed to GPRC5D.
Both have Phase III/registration programs, though BMS is more concentrated at this stage.
Both use small molecules, but the diseases and mechanisms are largely different.
Both have biologics, but with different disease and target focus.
Both have Phase III programs, without a clear same-indication collision.
Both have Phase II heart-failure programs, with different mechanisms.
Both portfolios are primarily small-molecule programs, but disease and target overlap is limited.
The heart-failure programs are both in Phase II.
Both have Phase III programs, but in different cardiovascular indications.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: Illustrative new-launch uptake scenario from the $3M H1 2026 starting point; not company guidance or consensus.
salesTrends.patentSummary: No product-specific loss-of-exclusivity date was disclosed in the 2025 Form 20-F; no cliff is applied through 2031.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: Illustrative new-launch uptake scenario from the $3M H1 2026 starting point; not company guidance or consensus.
salesTrends.patentSummary: No product-specific loss-of-exclusivity date was disclosed in the 2025 Form 20-F; no cliff is applied through 2031.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. Thereafter an illustrative slowing-growth curve is followed by modeled erosion beginning at the earliest disclosed 2032 exclusivity date.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Disclosed minimum exclusivity dates: US/China/EU 2032 and 2035; Japan 2034 and 2035. The scenario applies a cliff from 2032.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The scenario assumes continued indication growth through 2029, then erosion as disclosed EU/China and US exclusivity dates arrive.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Disclosed minimum exclusivity dates: China/EU 2030, US 2031 and Japan 2033. The scenario applies erosion from 2030.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The decline curve explicitly reflects the US loss of exclusivity reported in 2026 and the disclosed 2027 EU date.
salesTrends.patentSummary: US loss of exclusivity is already affecting 2026 results; the disclosed EU date is 2027, with additional regional patent layers extending later.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026 Opdivo plus Opdivo Qvantig. The scenario then applies material erosion at the disclosed US, EU and Japan exclusivity dates.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Disclosed minimum exclusivity dates for Opdivo: US 2028, EU 2030 and Japan 2031. The scenario applies sequential regional erosion.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. A base-case cliff begins around the currently listed 2033-2034 dates; pending patent-term/SPC extensions could delay the decline.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Current table: US 2034 and EU 2033; pending extensions could move US to 2036 and parts of Europe to 2038.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The scenario assumes continued uptake followed by erosion at the currently disclosed minimum exclusivity date.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Current minimum exclusivity is 2033 across the US, EU and Japan; a US patent-term-restoration application could extend to 2034.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The scenario uses a maturing growth curve and applies erosion at the disclosed US patent expiry.
salesTrends.patentSummary: US patent expiry is 2036; granted/pending extensions indicate 2038 in major European markets and 2039 in Japan.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The decline reflects unrestricted US generic entry from 31 January 2026 and existing generic competition outside the US.
salesTrends.patentSummary: US volume-limited generic licenses became unrestricted on 31 January 2026; generics are already present in Europe and Japan.

salesTrends.projectionBasis: 2026E annualizes H1 2026. The decline reflects expected US generic entry in Q1 2026 and existing European generic competition.
salesTrends.patentSummary: Generic entry was expected in the US in Q1 2026; generics are already present in Europe and the minimum Japanese exclusivity date is 2026.
